svg.title: MOSAIC single-grid CGRA architecture
svg.desc: One continuous rectangular mesh connects BCT, MST, VCT, SFT and CPT tiles. Every position contains a native tile and a local switch. Shared banked SRAM has host access and a dedicated MST memory bridge. The illustrated 2 by 3 placement follows the heterogeneous flavor example. Host, external data/memory and clock sources surround the CGRA. A dashed group identifies the proposed host-facing adapter; the grid and native interfaces follow existing RTL.

g.text: MOSAIC flat architecture · one R × C mesh · example placement includes all five tile types
Choose hardware, program contexts and routes
Launch work and collect results through the adapter
Application inputs, outputs and configuration images
One common functional clock / reset domain
Optional shared gate controls fabric clock activity
Program each local switch through its native ports
Allocate / start / suspend / drain native tiles
Activate committed contexts at safe points
Host SRAM access and native MST DMA streams
A platform adapter connects external memory
Collect completion / error records and status
Expose counters and platform interrupt policy
Grid exports native per-tile and route interfaces.
Host transport is selected by platform integration.
Neighbor links carry data through statically configured local switches.
Perimeter streams connect external data producers and consumers.
8 banks × 32 words × 8 B = 2,048 B · host client + one memory client per MST
Common mesh payload width follows the widest selected native tile.
FROM A HARDWARE FLAVOR TO EXECUTING DATAFLOW
Launch the native tiles; stream data
All tile positions belong to the same mesh. Hardware selection and runtime context programming are separate steps.
Grid and native tiles follow the Configurable backend. The dashed host-facing adapter is an integration concept.
Placement is logical connectivity. Silicon area, timing, power and energy require later technology-specific implementation.
